content.value_statement: Real-time features fail when streaming patterns omit backpressure, reconnection, and cleanup. This skill provides SSE, WebSocket, and ReadableStream patterns for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use SSE, WebSockets, and ReadableStream APIs.
Shows Next.js route handler examples for SSE responses.
Provides a reconnection class with exponential backoff.
Includes an SSE endpoint template and client wrapper.
Includes a checklist for SSE, WebSocket, backpressure, LLM streaming, and testing.
limitations: Examples are educational and need project-specific authentication and rate limits.
The skill does not deploy servers or run load tests.
The WebSocket example is minimal and omits production connection management.
LLM streaming examples may need updates for current provider SDKs.

use_cases.title: Design a streamed chat response
use_cases.description: Choose SSE or ReadableStream patterns for token delivery, completion markers, and client parsing.

use_cases.title: Add live application updates
use_cases.description: Implement server-to-client notifications with keepalive messages, reconnect behavior, and cleanup on disconnect.

use_cases.title: Review production readiness
use_cases.description: Use the checklist to evaluate authentication, message limits, backpressure, testing, and failure handling.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a streaming pattern
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new real-time feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: I am building [feature] with [traffic level]. Compare SSE, WebSockets, and ReadableStream, then recommend one pattern.

prompt_templates.title: Create an SSE endpoint
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate implementation for a web application.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Next.js SSE endpoint for [data source]. Include keepalive messages, disconnect cleanup, and client parsing steps.

prompt_templates.title: Improve stream reliability
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of reconnection and flow control.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this streaming design: [design]. Identify reconnection, timeout, backpressure, and resource cleanup gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a production stream
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this production streaming architecture: [architecture]. Cover authentication, rate limits, message validation, observability, and failure recovery.

output_examples.input: Ask which transport to use for a live notification feed.
output: Recommended transport: Server-Sent Events for one-way updates.
Key requirements: keepalive messages, automatic reconnect, and cleanup on disconnect.
Use WebSockets only if clients must send frequent real-time messages.

output_examples.input: Ask for a production checklist for streamed LLM responses.
output: Validate requests before starting the stream.
Handle partial text, disconnects, retries, and slow clients.
Measure time to first token and memory usage.

output_examples.input: Ask how to harden a WebSocket chat feature.
output_examples.output: The skill returns guidance for authentication, origin checks, heartbeat handling, reconnection, message limits, and content validation.

best_practices: Validate and authenticate every streaming connection before sending user data.
Design reconnection, timeout, and cleanup behavior before writing client code.
Test slow clients, interrupted networks, and concurrent connections early.
anti_patterns: Do not copy examples without adding authentication, authorization, and rate limits.
Do not stream raw error messages or unvalidated client content.
Do not ignore backpressure, browser connection limits, or cleanup on disconnect.

faq.question: What streaming methods does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Server-Sent Events, WebSockets, ReadableStream, reconnection logic, and LLM token streaming patterns.

faq.question: Is this skill only for Next.js?
faq.answer: No. The examples use Next.js, but the transport patterns apply to many streaming-capable web frameworks.

faq.question: Does it include production security controls?
faq.answer: It lists required controls, but teams must add authentication, authorization, origin checks, validation, and rate limits.

faq.question: Can it help choose between SSE and WebSockets?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains when one-way SSE is enough and when bidirectional WebSockets are a better fit.

faq.question: Does it support LLM streaming workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes patterns for streamed model responses, completion markers, client parsing, and response assembly.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is documented for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatible workflows.
